review.source: Actual written N1904 and the publisher rows, reviewed against the displayed BSB by Claude (Anthropic); independent peer review recorded in the registry.

17:1.sourceText: Ταῦτα ἐλάλησεν Ἰησοῦς, καὶ ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν εἶπεν Πάτερ, ἐλήλυθεν ἡ ὥρα· δόξασόν σου τὸν Υἱόν, ἵνα ὁ Υἱὸς δοξάσῃ σέ,
17:1.targetText: When Jesus had spoken these things, He lifted up His eyes to heaven and said, “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son may glorify You.

groups.note: BSB turns the καί-joined first clause into a When-clause.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English joins the participle clause to the main verb.

17:2.sourceText: καθὼς ἔδωκας αὐτῷ ἐξουσίαν πάσης σαρκός, ἵνα πᾶν ὃ δέδωκας αὐτῷ δώσῃ αὐτοῖς ζωὴν αἰώνιον.
17:2.targetText: For You granted Him authority over all people, so that He may give eternal life to all those You have given Him.

groups.note: The resumptive αὐτοῖς ("to them") supplies to; English names the recipients once as all those.

17:3.sourceText: αὕτη δέ ἐστιν ἡ αἰώνιος ζωὴ, ἵνα γινώσκωσιν σὲ τὸν μόνον ἀληθινὸν Θεὸν καὶ ὃν ἀπέστειλας Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν.
17:3.targetText: Now this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, whom You have sent.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:4.sourceText: ἐγώ σε ἐδόξασα ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, τὸ ἔργον τελειώσας ὃ δέδωκάς μοι ἵνα ποιήσω·
17:4.targetText: I have glorified You on earth by accomplishing the work You gave Me to do.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative pronoun ὅ ("that") is left implicit in English.

17:5.sourceText: καὶ νῦν δόξασόν με σύ, Πάτερ, παρὰ σεαυτῷ τῇ δόξῃ ᾗ εἶχον πρὸ τοῦ τὸν κόσμον εἶναι παρὰ σοί.
17:5.targetText: And now, Father, glorify Me in Your presence with the glory I had with You before the world existed.

groups.note: παρά with the dative ("beside") is rendered in … presence.
The dative τῇ δόξῃ is rendered with the glory.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the emphatic σύ ("you") unexpressed in the command.
The relative pronoun ᾗ ("which") is left implicit in English.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:6.sourceText: Ἐφανέρωσά σου τὸ ὄνομα τοῖς ἀνθρώποις οὓς ἔδωκάς μοι ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου. σοὶ ἦσαν κἀμοὶ αὐτοὺς ἔδωκας, καὶ τὸν λόγον σου τετήρηκαν.
17:6.targetText: I have revealed Your name to those You have given Me out of the world. They were Yours; You gave them to Me, and they have kept Your word.

groups.note: τοῖς ἀνθρώποις ("to the men") is rendered to those.
κἀμοί (καί + ἐμοί) is rendered to Me; BSB leaves its and unexpressed.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative pronoun οὕς ("whom") is left implicit in English.

17:7.sourceText: νῦν ἔγνωκαν ὅτι πάντα ὅσα δέδωκάς μοι παρὰ σοῦ εἰσιν·
17:7.targetText: Now they know that everything You have given Me comes from You.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative ὅσα ("as many as") is left implicit in English.

17:8.sourceText: ὅτι τὰ ῥήματα ἃ ἔδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἔλαβον, καὶ ἔγνωσαν ἀληθῶς ὅτι παρὰ σοῦ ἐξῆλθον, καὶ ἐπίστευσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
17:8.targetText: For I have given them the words You gave Me, and they have received them. They knew with certainty that I came from You, and they believed that You sent Me.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative pronoun ἅ ("which") is left implicit in English.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of received; the Greek verb has none.

17:9.sourceText: Ἐγὼ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐρωτῶ· οὐ περὶ τοῦ κόσμου ἐρωτῶ, ἀλλὰ περὶ ὧν δέδωκάς μοι, ὅτι σοί εἰσιν,
17:9.targetText: I ask on their behalf. I do not ask on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those You have given Me; for they are Yours.

17:10.sourceText: καὶ τὰ ἐμὰ πάντα σά ἐστιν καὶ τὰ σὰ ἐμά, καὶ δεδόξασμαι ἐν αὐτοῖς.
17:10.targetText: All I have is Yours, and all You have is Mine; and in them I have been glorified.

groups.note: ἐστιν is understood again with Mine.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English repeats all in the second half; the Greek has πάντα only in the first.

17:11.sourceText: καὶ οὐκέτι εἰμὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ εἰσίν, κἀγὼ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι. Πάτερ ἅγιε, τήρησον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν καθὼς ἡμεῖς.
17:11.targetText: I will no longer be in the world, but they are in the world, and I am coming to You.  Holy Father, protect them by Your name, the name You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one.

groups.note: ἕν is understood again in the comparison καθὼς ἡμεῖς.
κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered and I.
The relative ᾧ ("which") is rendered by repeating the name.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the verb in the comparison; the Greek says only "as we".

17:12.sourceText: ὅτε ἤμην μετ’ αὐτῶν, ἐγὼ ἐτήρουν αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ ὀνόματί σου ᾧ δέδωκάς μοι, καὶ ἐφύλαξα, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐξ αὐτῶν ἀπώλετο εἰ μὴ ὁ υἱὸς τῆς ἀπωλείας, ἵνα ἡ γραφὴ πληρωθῇ.
17:12.targetText: While I was with them, I protected and preserved them by Your name, the name You gave Me. Not one of them has been lost, except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture would be fulfilled.

groups.note: The relative ᾧ ("which") is rendered by repeating the name.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB starts a new sentence here instead of rendering καί.

17:13.sourceText: νῦν δὲ πρὸς σὲ ἔρχομαι, καὶ ταῦτα λαλῶ ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἵνα ἔχωσιν τὴν χαρὰν τὴν ἐμὴν πεπληρωμένην ἐν ἑαυτοῖς.
17:13.targetText: But now I am coming to You; and I am saying these things while I am in the world, so that they may have My joy fulfilled within them.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The repeated article before ἐμήν has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

unmappedTarget.reason: English makes in the world a clause; the Greek has no verb here.

17:14.sourceText: ἐγὼ δέδωκα αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον σου, καὶ ὁ κόσμος ἐμίσησεν αὐτούς, ὅτι οὐκ εἰσὶν ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.
17:14.targetText: I have given them Your word and the world has hated them; for they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:15.sourceText: οὐκ ἐρωτῶ ἵνα ἄρῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου, ἀλλ’ ἵνα τηρήσῃς αὐτοὺς ἐκ τοῦ πονηροῦ.
17:15.targetText: I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.

17:16.sourceText: ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου οὐκ εἰσὶν καθὼς ἐγὼ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἐκ τοῦ κόσμου.
17:16.targetText: They are not of the world, just as I am not of the world.

17:17.sourceText: ἁγίασον αὐτοὺς ἐν τῇ ἀληθείᾳ· ὁ λόγος ὁ σὸς ἀλήθειά ἐστιν.
17:17.targetText: Sanctify them by the truth; Your word is truth.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The repeated article before σός has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:18.sourceText: καθὼς ἐμὲ ἀπέστειλας εἰς τὸν κόσμον, κἀγὼ ἀπέστειλα αὐτοὺς εἰς τὸν κόσμον·
17:18.targetText: As You sent Me into the world, I have also sent them into the world.

groups.note: κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ, "I also") is rendered I … also.

17:19.sourceText: καὶ ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν ἐγὼ ἁγιάζω ἐμαυτόν, ἵνα ὦσιν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἡγιασμένοι ἐν ἀληθείᾳ.
17:19.targetText: For them I sanctify Myself, so that they too may be sanctified by the truth.

unmappedSource.reason: The opening καί only links to the previous verse.

17:20.sourceText: Οὐ περὶ τούτων δὲ ἐρωτῶ μόνον, ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῶν πιστευόντων διὰ τοῦ λόγου αὐτῶν εἰς ἐμέ,
17:20.targetText: I am not asking on behalf of them alone, but also on behalf of those who will believe in Me through their message,

unmappedSource.reason: BSB leaves the connective δέ untranslated.
The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.

17:21.sourceText: ἵνα πάντες ἓν ὦσιν, καθὼς σύ, Πατήρ, ἐν ἐμοὶ κἀγὼ ἐν σοί, ἵνα καὶ αὐτοὶ ἐν ἡμῖν ὦσιν, ἵνα ὁ κόσμος πιστεύῃ ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας.
17:21.targetText: that all of them may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I am in You. May they also be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.

groups.note: Same word, in a different form in BSB's Greek text.
κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered and I.
BSB renders this ἵνα clause ("that they may be") as the wish May they … be.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.
English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

17:22.sourceText: κἀγὼ τὴν δόξαν ἣν δέδωκάς μοι δέδωκα αὐτοῖς, ἵνα ὦσιν ἓν καθὼς ἡμεῖς ἕν·
17:22.targetText: I have given them the glory You gave Me, so that they may be one as We are one—

groups.note: κἀγώ (καί + ἐγώ) is rendered I; BSB leaves its and unexpressed.

unmappedSource.reason: The relative pronoun ἥν ("which") is left implicit in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the copula; the Greek clause has no verb.

17:23.sourceText: ἐγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς καὶ σὺ ἐν ἐμοί, ἵνα ὦσιν τετελειωμένοι εἰς ἕν, ἵνα γινώσκῃ ὁ κόσμος ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας καὶ ἠγάπησας αὐτοὺς καθὼς ἐμὲ ἠγάπησας.
17:23.targetText: I in them and You in Me—that they may be perfectly united, so that the world may know that You sent Me and have loved them just as You have loved Me.

groups.note: εἰς ἕν ("into one") is rendered united.

17:24.sourceText: Πατήρ, ὃ δέδωκάς μοι, θέλω ἵνα ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ κἀκεῖνοι ὦσιν μετ’ ἐμοῦ, ἵνα θεωρῶσιν τὴν δόξαν τὴν ἐμὴν, ἣν δέδωκάς μοι ὅτι ἠγάπησάς με πρὸ καταβολῆς κόσμου.
17:24.targetText: Father, I want those You have given Me to be with Me where I am, that they may see the glory You gave Me because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.

groups.note: Same word, in a different form in BSB's Greek text.
The headless relative ὅ ("what") stands for the group and is rendered those.

unmappedSource.reason: The resumptive κἀκεῖνοι ("and those") picks up those You have given Me; BSB names the group only once.
The repeated article before ἐμήν has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
BSB leaves ἐμήν ("My") unexpressed.
The relative pronoun ἥν ("which") is left implicit in English.

17:25.sourceText: Πατὴρ δίκαιε, καὶ ὁ κόσμος σε οὐκ ἔγνω, ἐγὼ δέ σε ἔγνων, καὶ οὗτοι ἔγνωσαν ὅτι σύ με ἀπέστειλας·
17:25.targetText: Righteous Father, although the world has not known You, I know You, and they know that You sent Me.

groups.note: Same word, in a different form in BSB's Greek text.

unmappedSource.reason: BSB expresses the contrast with although instead of a separate but.

17:26.sourceText: καὶ ἐγνώρισα αὐτοῖς τὸ ὄνομά σου καὶ γνωρίσω, ἵνα ἡ ἀγάπη ἣν ἠγάπησάς με ἐν αὐτοῖς ᾖ κἀγὼ ἐν αὐτοῖς.
17:26.targetText: And I have made Your name known to them and will continue to make it known, so that the love You have for Me may be in them, and I in them.”

groups.note: ἠγάπησας ("You loved") is rendered You have for, with love as the noun.

unmappedSource.reason: The actual article has no distinct counterpart in this English wording.
The relative pronoun ἥν ("which") is left implicit in English.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies the object of make known; the Greek verb has none.
